executive_preview: The clearest industry signal this week is a move from EV-only planning toward powertrain flexibility. Hyundai is expanding battery-electric vehicles while adding extended-range EVs, hybrids and combustion-powered products; Honda is considering making the Accord and CR-V hybrid-only; Volvo is increasing long-range PHEV emphasis; and UK policymakers are reviewing ZEV targets amid manufacturing-cost concerns. This is not a retreat from electrification, but a more pragmatic attempt to match product mix with consumer adoption, infrastructure and regional regulation.

lead_development.title: Performance differentiation is shifting from horsepower toward character and weight
lead_development.what_happened: Mercedes-AMG is using simulated engine sound and advanced torque vectoring in the electric CLA 45; Lotus is developing V6 and V8 hybrids with a 1.5-tonne target; Ferrari is reportedly testing a lighter, potentially non-hybrid 296 derivative; and Toyota is pursuing hybrid sports cars under an expanded GR brand.
lead_development.why_it_matters: As electric power makes extreme acceleration more accessible, premium performance brands are looking for differentiation through sound, mechanical engagement, low mass, aerodynamics and exclusivity. Ferrari's program remains unconfirmed, so it should be treated as a watch item rather than a confirmed strategy.

signals.title: Hyundai expands a multi-powertrain product offensive through 2030
signals.teaser: Hyundai and Genesis outlined a major launch program, including 41 new or refreshed models in Europe, 58 North American launches and more than 100 global launches or substantial updates by 2030.

signals.title: Automakers are repositioning hybrids and EREVs as adoption bridges
signals.teaser: Volvo said it will expand long-range PHEVs because pure-EV adoption is slower than expected.

signals.title: Battery manufacturing capacity is being redirected toward stationary storage
signals.teaser: Ford, GM and Tesla are expanding stationary battery-storage activities as EV demand and vehicle plans fall short of earlier expectations.

downside.title: Powertrain complexity may increase retail, service and residual-value uncertainty
downside.teaser: Automakers are expanding combinations of BEV, PHEV, EREV, hybrid and ICE products while software and battery systems become more sophisticated.

upside.title: Use EREVs and long-range PHEVs to expand electrified sales without requiring full BEV readiness
upside.teaser: Hyundai, Genesis and Volvo are positioning range-extended or long-range plug-in products as EV-like vehicles with reduced range anxiety.
